alloys.alloys_notes: The alloy is designated Fe-8Mn-6Al-0.2C (nominal), while Table 1 reports the measured chemical composition (wt%) of the investigated alloy: C 0.15, Mn 7.35, Al 6.00, P < 0.005, S 0.01, Fe balance. P and S are impurity elements. Cast in a vacuum induction furnace.
alloys.description: A medium-Mn (5-12%), medium-Al (1-8%) Fe-Mn-Al-C low density automotive steel designed to obtain a duplex ferrite + austenite microstructure via Al addition, studied for its TRIP effect and mechanical stability of retained austenite. Density 6.95 g/cm3, about 11% lower than pure iron.

source.reason: Identified as the single material system of the study: the abstract, introduction and conclusions repeatedly state the object is 'Fe-8Mn-6Al-0.2C low density steel', and Table 1 gives the chemical composition of the investigated alloy (C 0.15, Mn 7.35, Al 6.00, Fe bal.). All H70-H100 specimens are made from this one alloy, so only one alloy entity is defined.

paper.paper_scope: Investigates the microstructure and tensile behavior (work hardening, TRIP effect and austenite stability) of a Fe-8Mn-6Al-0.2C low density steel after solution treatment at 700-1000 °C for 1 h, correlating microstructural evolution with the mechanical properties of the four solution-treated states.
paper.title: A R T I C L E I N F O

processes.description: Hot-rolled steel sheet solution treated at 700 °C for 1 h followed by water quenching to room temperature.
processes.process_name: Solution treatment at 700 °C for 1 h + water quenching
processes.processes_notes: All four solution-treated states share the same prior thermo-mechanical processing: vacuum induction casting, heating at 1150 °C for 2 h, hot forging to 35 x 70 x 100 mm rods with air cooling, homogenization at 1200 °C for 2 h, hot rolling to 3 mm in 6 passes (start 1150 °C, finish 850 °C), water quenching to 550 °C, air cooling to room temperature.

source.reason: The specimens solution treated at 700, 800, 900 and 1000 °C for 1 h with water quenching are the four distinct terminal process states of the study, labeled H70-H100.

The Fe-8Mn-6Al-0.2C alloy solution treated at 700 °C for 1 h + water quenching is a distinct studied sample (label H70) with its own microstructure and tensile properties (UTS 778.3 MPa, TE 23%, f-gamma 12.2%).

The Fe-8Mn-6Al-0.2C alloy solution treated at 800 °C for 1 h + water quenching is a distinct studied sample (label H80) with its own microstructure and tensile properties (UTS 724.5 MPa, TE 30.5%, f-gamma 20.7%).
The Fe-8Mn-6Al-0.2C alloy solution treated at 900 °C for 1 h + water quenching is the principal studied sample (label H90), with best UTS 846.4 MPa and TE 32%, f-gamma 33.8%.
The Fe-8Mn-6Al-0.2C alloy solution treated at 1000 °C for 1 h + water quenching is a distinct studied sample (label H100) with highest UTS 860.3 MPa but lowest TE 15%, f-gamma 12.9%.

unmapped_findings: The tested steel has a measured density of 6.95 g/cm3, about 11% lower than pure iron (measured by densitometry based on Archimedes principle).
Austenite C content (XRD) and Mn/Al content (EDS) of austenite differ by specimen: H70 (C 0.556, Mn 8.91, Al 5.22 mass%), H80 (C 0.479, Mn 8.85, Al 5.1 mass%), H90 (C 0.391, Mn 8.34, Al 4.67 mass%).

Calculated martensitic transformation starting temperature Ms and Md30 differ by specimen: H70 Ms 33 °C, H80 Ms 67 °C, H90 Ms 120 °C; Md30 of H70 168 °C (also reported as 268 °C in text), H80 204 °C, H90 249 °C.
Solution-treated specimens were analyzed by SEM, TEM, EBSD and XRD; tensile specimens had a gauge width of 12.5 mm and gauge length of 50 mm machined along the longitudinal direction.
